```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
#we need the libs here
```
This is the h3 analysis, but instead of using the correlations as a covariate, we use a regressor that I made whihc uses the number of yes and no responses. 

This is less the standard so we did not end up going with this one. 

```{r h3}
trials <- seq(5,70,5)
Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>% 
  mutate(pearson.corr = cor(risk, gain, method = "pearson")) %>% 
  ungroup(user_id) %>% 
  dplyr::select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected, Yes, No, pearson.corr) %>% 
   mutate(experimental_treatment_selected = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) %>%
  #filter(gain == trials) %>% 
  mutate(YN_diff = Yes - No)-> test
#sensitivity analysis. By only choosing trials where sample both gains and lossess equally, we get risks that are larger than gains; intresting

continuous <- c("risk", "gain", "YN_diff")

test[,continuous] <- scale(test[,continuous])  
#model 1 only linear terms
#cl <- makePSOCKcluster() #use parallel processing

registerDoParallel()
#start with risk, and gain
m.1 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + risk + gain  +
               (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
             data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 0)

#add poly gain
m.2 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + risk + gain + I(gain^2) +
               (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
             data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 0)
#just add poly risk 
m.3 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) + 
               (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
             data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 0)
#linear interaction
m.4 <-  glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + 
                risk + gain + 
                I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) + 
                risk:gain + 
                (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
              data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
              control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
              nAGQ = 0)
#next interaction
m.5 <-  glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + 
                risk + gain +
                I(risk^2) + I(gain^2)+
                risk:gain+
                risk:I(gain^2) +
                (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
              data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
              control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
              nAGQ = 0)

m.6 <-  glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + 
                risk + gain +
                I(risk^2) + I(gain^2)+
                risk:gain+
                risk:I(gain^2) +
                gain:I(risk^2) + 
                (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
              data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
              control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
              nAGQ = 0)

m.7 <-  glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ YN_diff + 
                risk + gain +
                I(risk^2) + I(gain^2)+
                risk:gain+
                risk:I(gain^2) +
                gain:I(risk^2) + 
                I(risk^2):I(gain^2)+
                (risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2)| user_id), 
              data = test, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
              control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
              nAGQ = 0)

table <-anova(m.1, m.2, m.3, m.4, m.5, m.6, m.7, type = "LRT")
tab <- map_df(list(table), tidy)
options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "npar", "AIC", "BIC", "logLik", "deviance", "statistic", 
                   "df", "p.value")], caption = "Model Comparison")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")
##
Anova(m.6, type = "III")
ggeffects::ggpredict(m.6, terms=c("risk", "gain"))

stopImplicitCluster()
```

```{r h3 plots}
library(ggpubr)

p1 <- plot(ggeffects::ggpredict(m.6, terms=c("risk [all]", "gain")))+ 
  geom_hline(yintercept = .50)
p2 <- plot(ggeffects::ggpredict(m.6, terms=c("gain [all]", "risk")))+ 
  geom_hline(yintercept = .50)

parameters::model_parameters(m.6) %>% 
  filter(!Parameter == "(Intercept)")->x
kable(x[c("Parameter", "Coefficient", "SE", "CI_low", "CI_high", "z", "p")])%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")


p3 <- ggstatsplot::ggcoefstats(m.6,
point.args = list(color = "red", size = 3, shape = 15),
  vline.args = list(size = 1, color = "#CC79A7", linetype = "dotdash"),
  title = "Logistic mixed model predicting experimental treatment selected",
  ggstatsplot.layer = FALSE
) 
ggarrange(p1, p2, 
          labels = c("A", "B"),
          ncol = 2, nrow = 1)
#m.6 %>% broom.mixed::augment() ->d
#report(m.6)
```

**Table 1:** main effects across all models
```{r printLM table risk, echo=FALSE}
tab_model(m.1, m.2, m.3,m.4, m.5, m.6,
          digits = 4, 
          show.df = T, 
          show.stat = T, 
          string.pred = "Ind. Variable", 
          col.order = c("est","ci","df","stat","p"), 
          dv.labels = c("Model 1", "Model 2","Model 3", "Model 4", "Model 5","Model 6")
          )
```
*Note:* Standardized parameters were obtained by fitting the model on a standardized version of the dataset. 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p-values were computed using the Wald approximation.
